findings.claim: The new wrapper around reportAnalyzerDiagnostic silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. Diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None) were previously reported and are now filtered out. Examples include MemberNeedsKey, now built with FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), and any other diagnostic created without a location. Users who rely on these analyzer diagnostics, including warnings-as-errors, could stop seeing them. This is wider than the crash fix.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/006/007/008/009/010/011/012/013/014/015/016/017/018 suites) with the head build. Add a case where a diagnostic is raised with a Location.None or a location from another tree, and assert whether it is still reported compared with base.

findings.claim: The two guards `contractAttr is not null && !formattedType.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty` skip the derived-Key-attribute / MemberNeedsKey branch whenever the type has no syntax. This only avoids the crash. For a metadata type the diagnostic no longer fires, which is consistent with L8. However, the guard tests formattedType, not item. For a partial type or a type spread across trees, behaviour is unchanged. Members inherited from a metadata base class into a source-declared type now still enter this branch, and item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty there. The MemberNeedsKey location becomes null, and the wrapper then drops the diagnostic. That is a silent change in reporting.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] class in source derives from a metadata base class with a public property lacking [Key]. Compare the MsgPack004 diagnostics reported on base and on head.
